5: # Work with fr

{"text": "1: # Explore only the needed structure
2: 
3: The examples use a project containing `app.py`. Substitute the relevant path in the real task.
4: Keep the repository as the scan root when callers elsewhere matter; a single-file `-C` restricts discovery to that file.
5: 
6: ```sh
7: fr project find greet --in app.py --signature --limit 12
8: fr project select greet render validate --signature --source --bytes 2048
9: fr project show '<HANDLE>'
10: fr project show '<HANDLE>' --relations --limit 8
11: fr project show '<HANDLE>' --source --bytes 256
12: fr project calls '<HANDLE>' --direction incoming --limit 8
13: fr project tests app.py --limit 8
14: fr project features --limit 12
15: fr project gaps --limit 8
16: ```
17: 
18: When the task needs several views, use the bounded manifest in [Batch](batch.md).
19: 
20: Use exact `project find NAME` for known declarations. Add the boolean `--contains` flag for a literal substring; it takes no value.
21: Find matches names before clipping and reports all candidates with pagination and source coverage.
22: Use `project select SELECTOR...` for several exact names or full handles so one revision,
23: coverage report, cursor and source budget cover the complete request. Read every per-selector
24: status before claiming absence. Handles select one exact node and can report `outside-scope`,
25: `not-a-declaration` or an omitted local; stale handles refuse instead of becoming names.
26: Use maps when the hierarchy itself matters. Choose `<HANDLE>` from the relevant declaration row. Full handles include their source revision.
27: Alternatively use a short ID with the returned `--revision`; never reuse a bare ID across revisions.
28: `show` gives the declaration's `position`, a 1-based line and column suitable for a refactoring target.
29: Its syntax header can contain defaults and attributes; it is not a complete semantic contract.
30: 
31: Request `--source` only when needed. Source offsets count bytes from the selected node's start, not lines or file-relative offsets.
32: For another slice, pass the returned `next_offset` with `--offset`; this preserves UTF-8 boundaries.
33: For another result page, reuse the same query and fields with `--cursor` and the returned `page.next`.
34: Changing source, manifests, scan options or query scope can invalidate a handle or cursor. Restart the relevant map or query after a stale response.
35: 
36: Maps show lexical containment, not inferred architecture.
37: Call results preserve confidence and unresolved or dispatch-candidate rows; candidates do not establish runtime dispatch.
38: Test associations are candidates for selecting checks, not proof of complete coverage or commands to execute blindly.
39: Use `project packages`, `dependencies`, `links` and `workspaces` for manifest declarations and local relationships when package boundaries matter.
40: Use `project routes`, `contracts` and `configuration` for their supported declaration patterns when the task needs those views.
41: Use `project features` for the parent-linked Next.js App Router or FastAPI application, package, route, handler, contract, execution-dependency, middleware and schema hierarchy.
42: Pass a returned `--feature ID` to retrieve one revision-bound subtree.
43: Middleware order and direct FastAPI providers are syntax candidates; inspect their source before making runtime or authentication claims.
44: Lifecycle, configuration and service facts also retain syntax evidence and explicit runtime gaps.
45: Service targets omit query strings, fragments and URL credentials; use a source slice only when the task needs request details.
46: Next.js page features include inherited layouts and bounded direct relative component imports.
47: Their React facts cover props, hooks, events, styles and render edges.
48: Unique same-file, default-import and named-import render targets include a source anchor; inspect unresolved targets directly.
49: These commands do not establish complete dependency resolution or framework semantics.

{"text": "1: # Author selected code
2: 
3: `fr author` has `replace-body`, `replace-declaration`, `insert-declaration`, and `batch`;
4: batches accept up to 32 disjoint steps including `organize-imports`. Coordinate callers after
5: signature changes. Unsupported targets refuse.
6: 
7: Use `fr author guide` for machine-readable operations, limits and transitions. After reading
8: this route, skip subcommand help.
9: 
10: For several exact declarations, use one `project select NAME... --source`; duplicate names
11: across files return together. Use `project find NAME --in FILE --source` for one declaration;
12: `root` is its file handle. A module/trait row selects that container; a direct method selects
13: its impl/trait. Otherwise use
14: `project map FILE --depth 0 --fields handle,kind,name --limit 1`. Source changes expire handles.
15: 
16: UTF-8 fragments are limited to 64 KiB. Steps need `op` and `handle`; fragment steps add
17: `from`, short IDs need top-level `revision`, and `organize-imports` takes a file handle. Steps
18: use original source; overlaps refuse. Exact `postconditions`: `files-changed`, `edits`,
19: `changed-operations`, and `paths-changed`.
20: Paths are project-relative. Copy absolute paths from external artifact writers verbatim into
21: fragment `from` fields and batch `--from`.
22: 
23: Review the complete diff and retain `plan_context_basis`. Repeat it with
24: `--save-plan --plan-basis BASIS`; drift or clipping refuses before persistence. The result's
25: `transaction_context_basis` compacts forward application. `plan_context_basis` starts with
26: `frpb1`; `frcb1` is a project basis and cannot save a plan.
27: 
28: Rust insertion preserves bytes and doc comments; only traits allow bodyless functions. Body
29: replacement covers Rust, Go, Java, and supported TypeScript/TSX bindings; arrows may change form.
30: 
31: ```rust
32: /// Increments a value twice.
33: pub fn increment_twice(value: u32) -> u32 {
34:     increment(increment(value))
35: }
36: ```
37: Use the lookup's file-scoped `root` as `<FILE_HANDLE>`:
38: ```sh
39: fr project find increment --in src/lib.rs --source --bytes 512
40: fr author batch --from '<MANIFEST>'
41: fr author batch --from '<MANIFEST>' --save-plan --plan-basis '<PLAN_CONTEXT_BASIS>'
42: fr history apply '<AUTHOR_TX>' --write --no-diff --context-basis '<TRANSACTION_CONTEXT_BASIS>'
43: ```
44: Continue source with `next_offset`. Run [checks](checks.md); retain the transaction for [history](history.md) and [patch export](git.md).
", "total_lines": 44, "next_line": null}

I’ll add documented APIs in both crates and replace that constructor with an exact escaped-length precomputation.
